answer: Reputation decays exponentially with a fixed temporal half-life, requiring sustained, reciprocal honest service to keep trust from fading. In the EigenTrust graph, a freshly spawned Sybil has few credible incoming endorsements and thus near-zero eigenvector centrality; reciprocity-weighted transitivity cannot instantly amplify fabricated links. Like a pearl forming slowly in a river, trust accrues over time, and attempts to wander between identities cannot bypass consensus thresholds.
